This essentially unsocial element, created by the Revolution, will some day absorb the middle classes, just as the middle classes have destroyed the nobility.

28777-harper-s-young-people-april-6-1880.creator: Unknown
28777-harper-s-young-people-april-6-1880.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. But Charley had never loaded a gun before in all his life. Still, it was a very simple piece of business, and he knew all about it. He had read of it and heard it talked of ever so many times, and there was Jim loading his own gun within ten feet, just as if he meant to show how it should be done.

arxiv-1810-13225.title: Additive Manufactured and Topology Optimized Permanent Magnet Spin-Rotator for Neutron Interferometry Applications
arxiv-1810-13225.creator: Wenzel Kersten 1, Laurids Brandl 1, Richard Wagner 1, Christian Huber 2,3, Florian Bruckner 2,3, Yuji Hasegawa 1,4, Dieter Suess 2,3, Stephan Sponar 1
arxiv-1810-13225.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Wenzel Kersten 1, Laurids Brandl 1, Richard Wagner 1, Christian Huber 2,3, Florian Bruckner 2,3, Yuji Hasegawa 1,4, Dieter Suess 2,3, Stephan Sponar 1. In neutron interferometric experiments using polarized neutrons coherent spin-rotation control is required. In this letter we present a new method for Larmor spin-rotation around an axis parallel to the outer guide field using topology optimized 3D printed magnets.

arxiv-2201-09942.title: Many-Body Effects in the X-ray Absorption Spectra of Liquid Water
arxiv-2201-09942.creator: Fujie Tang, Zhenglu Li, Chunyi Zhang, Steven G. Louie, Roberto Car, Diana Y. Qiu, Xifan Wu
arxiv-2201-09942.description: Abstract X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) is a powerful experimental technique to probe the local order in materials with core electron excitations. Experimental interpretation requires supporting theoretical calculations. For water, these calculations are very demanding and, to date, could only be done with major approximations that limited the accuracy of the calculated spectra.

arxiv-2208-06124.title: Gradient Estimation for Binary Latent Variables via Gradient Variance Clipping
arxiv-2208-06124.creator: Russell Z. Kunes, Mingzhang Yin, Max Land, Doron Haviv, Dana Pe’er, Simon Tavaré
arxiv-2208-06124.description: Abstract Gradient estimation is often necessary for fitting generative models with discrete latent variables, in contexts such as reinforcement learning and variational autoencoder (VAE) training. The DisARM estimator (Yin et al. 2020; Dong, Mnih, and Tucker 2020) achieves state of the art gradient variance for Bernoulli latent variable models in many contexts.

arxiv-2212-04048.title: Executing your Commands via Motion Diffusion in Latent Space
arxiv-2212-04048.creator: Xin Chen, Biao Jiang, Wen Liu, Zilong Huang, Bin Fu, Tao Chen, Gang Yu
arxiv-2212-04048.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xin Chen, Biao Jiang, Wen Liu, Zilong Huang, Bin Fu, Tao Chen, Gang Yu. We study a challenging task, conditional human motion generation, which produces plausible human motion sequences according to various conditional inputs, such as action classes or textual descriptors. Since human motions are highly diverse and have a property of quite different distribution from conditional modalities, such as textual descriptors in natural languages, it is hard to learn a probabilistic mapping from the desired conditional modality to the human motion sequences.

arxiv-2311-03281.title: The separate-universe approach and sudden transitions during inflation
arxiv-2311-03281.creator: David Wands
arxiv-2311-03281.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by David Wands. The separate-universe approach gives an intuitive way to understand the evolution of cosmological perturbations in the long-wavelength limit. It uses solutions of the spatially-homogeneous equations of motion to model the evolution of the inhomogeneous universe on large scales. We show that the separate-universe approach fails on a finite range of super-Hubble scales at a sudden transition from slow roll to ultra-slow roll during inflation in the very early universe.

arxiv-2312-01301.title: Churn Prediction via Multimodal Fusion Learning: Integrating Customer Financial Literacy, Voice, and Behavioral Data
arxiv-2312-01301.creator: 1 st David Hason Rudd, 2 nd Huan Huo, 3 rd Md Rafiqul Islam, 4 rd Guandong Xu
arxiv-2312-01301.description: Abstract In today’s competitive landscape, businesses grapple with customer retention. Churn prediction models, although beneficial, often lack accuracy due to the reliance on a single data source. The intricate nature of human behavior and high-dimensional customer data further complicate these efforts.

arxiv-2312-09903.title: Topological magnon gap engineering in van der Waals CrI 3 ferromagnets
arxiv-2312-09903.creator: Verena Brehm, Pawel Sobieszczyk, Jostein N. Kløgetvedt, Richard F. L. Evans, Elton J. G. Santos, Alireza Qaiumzadeh
arxiv-2312-09903.description: Abstract The microscopic origin of the topological magnon band gap in CrI 3 ferromagnets has been a subject of controversy for years since two main models with distinct characteristics, i.e., Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) and Kitaev, provided possible explanations with different outcome implications.

arxiv-2404-02023.title: On the Regret of Recursive Methods for Discrete-Time Adaptive Control with Matched Uncertainty
arxiv-2404-02023.creator: Aren Karapetyan, Efe C. Balta, Anastasios Tsiamis, Andrea Iannelli, John Lygeros
arxiv-2404-02023.description: Abstract Continuous-time adaptive controllers for systems with a matched uncertainty often comprise an online parameter estimator and a corresponding parameterized controller to cancel the uncertainty. However, such methods are often impossible to implement directly , as they depend on an unobserved estimation error.

arxiv-2407-14364.title: Towards Assessing Data Replication in Music Generation with Music Similarity Metrics on Raw Audio
arxiv-2407-14364.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by . Recent advancements in music generation are raising multiple concerns about the implications of AI in creative music processes, current business models and impacts related to intellectual property management. A relevant discussion and related technical challenge is the potential replication and plagiarism of the training set in AI-generated music, which could lead to misuse of data and intellectual property rights violations.

arxiv-2408-02456.title: Enhancing Heterogeneous Knowledge Graph Completion with a Novel GAT-based Approach
arxiv-2408-02456.creator: Wanxu Wei, Yitong Song, Bin Yao
arxiv-2408-02456.description: Abstract . Knowledge graphs (KGs) play a vital role in enhancing search results and recommendation systems. With the rapid increase in the size of the KGs, they are becoming inaccuracy and incomplete. This problem can be solved by the knowledge graph completion methods, of which graph attention network (GAT)-based methods stand out since their superior performance.

arxiv-2501-09967.title: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI): from inherent explainability to large language models
arxiv-2501-09967.creator: Fuseini Mumuni, Alhassan Mumuni
arxiv-2501-09967.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Fuseini Mumuni, Alhassan Mumuni. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has continued to achieve tremendous success in recent times. However, the decision logic of these frameworks is often not transparent, making it difficult for stakeholders to understand, interpret or explain their behavior. This limitation hinders trust in machine learning systems and causes a general reluctance towards their adoption in practical applications, particularly in mission-critical domains like healthcare and autonomous driving.

pmc-10518342.title: Coinfection of pulmonary tuberculosis and mucormycosis in a patient with poor controlled diabetes mellitus: A case report
pmc-10518342.creator: Mehran shahanikelaki, Mohammad Mohammadi, Aynaz Mohammadi, Vahan Moradians
pmc-10518342.description: Coinfection of pulmonary mucormycosis and tuberculosis is a rare and challenging condition, particularly in immunocompromised patients. We present the case of a 60-year-old woman with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus who developed dysphonia, persistent cough, and expectoration. Imaging studies revealed a cavitary lesion and a mass in the left lung, along with stenosis of the left main bronchus.

pmc-10638428.title: High pretransplant FGF23 level is associated with persistent vitamin D insufficiency and poor graft survival in kidney transplant patients
pmc-10638428.creator: Jung-Hwa Ryu, Hee Jung Jeon, Ro Han, Hee-Yeon Jung, Myung-Gyu Kim, Kyu Ha Huh, Jae Berm Park, Kyung Pyo Kang, Seungyeup Han, Jaeseok Yang
pmc-10638428.description: Vitamin D3 (25[OH]D3) insufficiency and fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) elevation are usually attenuated after kidney transplantation (KT). However, elevated FGF23 may be associated with poor graft outcomes and vitamin D insufficiency after KT. This study investigated the effect of pretransplant FGF23 levels on post-KT 25(OH)D3 status and graft outcomes.

pmc-11320492.title: Investigation of diaphragmatic motion and projected lung area in diaphragm paralysis patients using dynamic chest radiography
pmc-11320492.creator: Ziyang Xia, Chuming Peng, Liyuan Fan, Qiongzhu Chen, Wentao Liu, Ting Ma, Weicong Chen, Yaocheng Wen, Yuquan Song, Haibo Lin
pmc-11320492.description: BackgroundDynamic chest radiography (DCR) is a novel and supplementary examination in respiratory diseases. The investigation of other chest diseases using DCR has been explored, identifying a certain correlation of the pulmonary function test (PFT). However, there is a lack of research using DCR parameters to quantitatively evaluate chest disease.

pmc-11504386.title: First Investigation of a Eustachian Tube Stent in Experimentally Induced Eustachian Tube Dysfunction
pmc-11504386.creator: Katharina Schmitt, Malena Timm, Philipp Krüger, Niels Oppel, Alexandra Napp, Friederike Pohl, Robert Schuon, Lisa Kötter, Marion Bankstahl, Thomas Lenarz, Tobias Stein, Gerrit Paasche
pmc-11504386.description: Unmet needs in the treatment of chronic otitis media and Eustachian tube dysfunction (ETD) triggered the development of stents for the Eustachian tube (ET). In this study, for the first time, stents were placed in an artificially blocked ET to evaluate stent function. Eight adult female sheep were injected with stabilized hyaluronic acid (HA) on both sides to induce ETD.

pmc-12388736.title: Separation of the Biofuel Methyl Ethyl Ketone from Aqueous Solutions Using Avocado-Based Activated Carbons: Synthesis Conditions and Multilayer Adsorption Properties
pmc-12388736.creator: Hilda Elizabeth Reynel-Avila, Eduardo Ledea-Figueredo, Lizbeth Liliana Díaz-Muñoz, Adrián Bonilla-Petriciolet, Ismael Alejandro Aguayo-Villarreal, Laura Gabriela Elvir-Padilla, Carlos Javier Durán-Valle
pmc-12388736.description: This study reports the separation of methyl ethyl ketone (MEK), a relevant compound in the biorefinery context, from aqueous solutions using activated carbons derived from avocado seed biomass. Two synthesis routes were explored via chemical and thermal activation with H2SO4 and KOH. A Taguchi experimental design was applied to tailor synthesis conditions, with MEK adsorption capacity as the target property.

pmc-12751158.title: Effects of acute static stretching and dynamic warm-up protocols on shoulder function in young adult male athletes with shoulder impingement syndrome: a randomized controlled crossover trial
pmc-12751158.creator: Mohammad Alghosi, Maryam Abduljabbar Khudhair, Mohammed Sadique K, Fereshteh Ejlali, Mojtaba Iranmanesh, Mohammad Alimoradi, Nicola Relph, Ali Shamsi Majelan
pmc-12751158.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundShoulder impingement syndrome (SIS) is common among overhead athletes. Static stretching (SS) and dynamic warm-up (DW) are widely used, but their acute effects on comprehensive shoulder function in athletes with SIS are not fully understood.

pmc-13196314.title: Unique repair of a mycotic extent IV thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm using a visceral branching technique with previous axillobifemoral bypass minimizing ischemia time
pmc-13196314.creator: Michael Youngjin Lee, Seyed Pairawan, Mouhammad Halabi, Alexander Shepard, Loay Kabbani, Andi Peshkepija
pmc-13196314.description: This case study demonstrates visceral branching approach for a mycotic type IV thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm in a 78-year-old man with previous axillobifemoral bypass. He underwent debridement, resection, and repair with a visceral branching technique using a modified rifampin-soaked bifurcated Dacron graft with perfusion catheters inserted into the visceral arteries. Contemporary repair involves aortic cross-clamping, producing significant hemodynamic effects.

pmc-13384658.title: Postoperative symptom cluster classification and its association with health-related quality of life in knee osteoarthritis patients after total knee arthroplasty: An observational study
pmc-13384658.creator: Lei Zhou, Xingren Chen, Qingxi Zhang, Tong Chen
pmc-13384658.description: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is an effective surgical treatment for advanced knee osteoarthritis (KOA). However, the classification of postoperative symptom clusters and their impact on quality of life (QoL) remain underexplored. This study aims to categorize symptom clusters in KOA patients after TKA using latent class analysis (LCA) and to analyze the relationship between symptom clusters and QoL.
